commit.message: feat(loop-closure): hardening lane v2 — propose/deliver trust split

intent: PR-E v2 of the walking-mode loop-closure plan. PR #1162 built the hardening lane as one process: agent, tests, commit and push in a single checkout holding contents:write. Fourteen review findings reduced to one fact — the agent and the delivery step shared a machine, filesystem, UID and process namespace, so every guard was a point-in-time check in a space the adversary could still write to, and Greptile's T-Rex drove a real git push to an attacker repository through the full guard set. The measured limit: `git -c` overrides single-valued keys, but credential.helper and url.BASE.insteadOf are multi-valued, so -c only appends and the hostile entry survives. This packet replaces mitigation with dissolution: a propose job with permissions contents:read and persist-credentials:false runs the agent and emits a git bundle; a separate deliver job on a separate runner verifies that bundle against origin and pushes. Delivery never runs agent code, never runs the suite, never checks out the candidate tree, and never stages.

negative_controls.command: python3 -c "import subprocess,sys; from pathlib import Path; p=Path('.github/workflows/hardening-lane.yml'); orig=p.read_text(); mut=orig.replace('      contents: read   # public repo: worth no more than an anonymous fetch','      contents: write',1); assert mut!=orig, 'propose permission line not found'; p.write_text(mut); r=subprocess.run([sys.executable,'-m','pytest','tests/test_lane_deliver.py','-q'],check=False); p.write_text(orig); sys.exit(0 if r.returncode!=0 else 2)"
negative_controls.name: granting-propose-write-breaks-the-trust-split-test

negative_controls.command: python3 -c "import subprocess,sys; from pathlib import Path; p=Path('scripts/runtime/lane_deliver.py'); orig=p.read_text(); mut=orig.replace('    forbidden = denied_paths(paths)','    forbidden = []',1); assert mut!=orig, 'denylist call not found'; p.write_text(mut); r=subprocess.run([sys.executable,'-m','pytest','tests/test_lane_deliver.py','-q'],check=False); p.write_text(orig); sys.exit(0 if r.returncode!=0 else 2)"
negative_controls.name: disabling-referee-denylist-breaks-delivery-tests

honest_blockers: First live run still requires the operator to configure the DHARMA_LANE_AGENT_CMD repo secret; without it the propose job refuses with a BLOCKED receipt instead of improvising an agent.
The mailbox ready-set selection activates only where the loop-tasks branch carries tasks; otherwise selection falls through to the failing-nightly probe or a NO_WORK receipt.

This is a Tier-2 change (.github/workflows/**): operator hand-merge only, and it is opened as a draft for that reason. Scheduled runs fire only from main, so the first live receipt is provable post-merge only.

The agent still authors the content. The split removes the credential, not the authorship: a hostile change set can be proposed, but only ever as a capped draft PR outside the referee paths, with CI and human review ahead of it.

The merge-base --is-ancestor check in lane_deliver.py is a redundant backstop today — the one-commit rule already implies it — and is retained only against a future relaxation of that rule. tests/test_lane_deliver.py states this explicitly rather than claiming an independent gate.
session_entry.rollback: Revert the single commit: both lane drivers, the two-job workflow, and the tests disappear. Any lane branches or draft PRs already opened remain inert drafts the operator can close.
